answer: Retrospective Correlation Roundup. Agents are clustered post hoc by behavioral fingerprints—shared timing offsets, near-identical action sequences, linked funding graphs—forming a ridge of correlated identities. Any cluster exceeding a threshold of mutually correlated accounts has its gains clawed back and future rewards pooled. A lone attacker must simulate distinct latency, spend patterns, and funding origins per identity, a timber of manual overhead per account. Collateral losses scale because one detected node exposes the lotus of the whole cluster.
